recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow current-build correction that preserves the FHIR-5816 guidance while aligning it with the later applied CompartmentDefinition membership semantics from FHIR-51725.
issue_request: FHIR-5816 was Published/Persuasive for DSTU1 and asked the specification to document that servers decide whether to include resources in compartments when the reference establishing the relationship is carried by an extension.
initial_application: Jira records svn 4610 as adding the requested note to extras.html. Git history confirms commit 4981f29411d5822e11c377e2f276548abf43d35a added the exact note to source/extras.html, and later source refactors carried it into source/compartmentdefinition/compartmentdefinition-notes.xml.
additional_context: CompartmentDefinition is an active resource in source/fhir.ini. Later applied issue FHIR-51725 and supporting Zulip/Confluence evidence clarified that resources are formally in a compartment through CompartmentDefinition.resource.param search parameters; resources outside the compartment may still be returned by _include or local convention at server discretion. That later context made the old 'include resources in a compartment' wording stale for extension references.
reconciliation: Changed source/compartmentdefinition/compartmentdefinition-notes.xml to say servers decide whether to make resources available through compartment-based retrieval operations when the reference to the compartment resource is in an extension, and that such resources are not formally part of the compartment unless the CompartmentDefinition identifies a search parameter for the relationship.
source_changes: source/compartmentdefinition/compartmentdefinition-notes.xml: reworded the extension-reference compartment note to use compartment-based retrieval availability wording and to tie formal membership to CompartmentDefinition search parameters.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Applied clarification about whether compartment inclusion is element- or search-based; its documentation-based inclusion wording was later revised by FHIR-51725.
Later Applied decision clarifying that compartment membership is search-parameter based while non-member resources may still be returned at server discretion.
